title: Action code changed to dump the runner's memory into the log
note: Modelled as a diff of the action's own action.yml, which is what upstream review (roadmap) would see. Users of the action saw no change in their own files; payload simplified.

title: Fake 'Github Actions Security' workflow pushed straight to the default branch
delivery: direct push with stolen credentials (no pull request)
note: Reconstructed from the public description: lists the secret names used by real pipelines and posts the values over plain HTTP. Caught only if PipeDelta also runs on push.

title: Workflow edited to mint cloud OIDC tokens, send all secrets out, then delete its own run
delivery: direct push with stolen tokens, followed by 'ci: cleanup' commits
note: Shape reconstructed from the public summary (OIDC minting, gzipped exfiltration, trace removal); exact payload not public.

title: New workflow added by a stolen token prints every secret, double-encoded, into the log
delivery: workflow created on the default branch by a pull_request_target token with write access
note: Stage 3 of the campaign. No network call: secrets are read back from public logs.

title: Workflow that outsiders can start gains the power to add the approval label
note: Models the label-gate bypass: once a pull_request_target workflow can label, the 'safe-to-test' gate can be self-applied.

title: Workflow that outsiders can start gains OIDC identity, enabling trusted publishing
note: The attack stole the runner's OIDC token and swapped it for npm publishing rights. This case is the configuration change that makes it possible.

title: Branch name pasted into a shell command in a pull_request_target workflow
note: The bot exploited branch and file names reaching run: blocks. Also the Ultralytics entry point (2024).

title: Build cache turned on in a workflow that outsiders can start
note: The attacker poisoned the cache from a pull_request_target run; the release job restored it and shipped a cryptominer to PyPI.

title: Discussion title and body pasted into a shell command
note: Anyone who opens a discussion containing $(...) runs code on the runner.
